messages:
erin: getting alert from us-west at 05:42 UTC: spike in TLS handshake failures for internal svc calls. early traces show cert fetch failures + KMS unwrap 403s. anyone touching RBAC or KMS aliases overnight?
carlos: i pushed a housekeeping RBAC change at 04:50 that added infra:auditor to a few namespaces, small change. no KMS alias work from me. logs?
em: can you post a redacted proxy/keystore log sample? trying to triage whether this is client cert validation or key unwrap
erin: pasted redacted logs below:
```
edge-proxy[edge-71]: 2026-06-11T05:42:12Z warn: tls: client auth failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority client=svc-account:ingestor-us
keystore-rotator[rotator]: 2026-06-11T05:42:12Z error: unwrap failed key=projects/redwood/keys/serving-main err=403 KMSDecryptDenied principal=svc-account:ingestor-us
```
may: audit trail shows two policy ops around 04:48-04:52 UTC: 1) an RBAC role-binding merged adding infra:auditor (carlos) 2) a policy PR that introduced a high-precedence deny rule for keystore:unwrap for non-prod accounts merged at 04:49, intended to block dev credentials. looks like a logic overlap where infra:auditor is a group that includes some runtime SAs in older namespaces due to legacy mapping
carlos: oh crap, the infra:auditor group mapping was broader than i realized. the deny rule’s intent was fine but precedence is killing critical runtime unwraps when both apply. sometimes the control-plane evaluates deny first, sometimes allow depending on replica reconciliation -> flapping 200/403
lina: immediate mitigations: 1) roll back the deny policy PR to stop high-precedence denies 2) add an explicit allow RoleBinding for svc-account:ingestor-us to keystore-decrypt for 1h 3) enable decision-level audit for key operations for 2h to get full decision_id chain
oncall: rolling back deny PR now (git revert + deploy). patching RBAC allow for ingestor-us. ETA ~4m
sec-bot: alert: keystore-decrypt-failures exceeded threshold at 2026-06-11T05:44:00Z. incident INC-190246 opened
may: suggest short-term KMS grant as well while control-plane fully reconciles, with a strict expiry (2026-06-11T07:00Z). this avoids multi-replica race windows where one replica still enforces deny
carlos: applying KMS grant ttl=1h for principal=svc-account:ingestor-us now. also updating infra group mapping to remove runtime SAs — will follow up w/ PR to tighten group scopes
erin: monitoring shows handshake failures dropping; rotator logs show unwrap success after ~90s of propagation. thanks team.
lina: follow-ups (SEC ticket SEC-2026-399): 1) tighten infra group mappings and document exclusions for runtime SAs 2) make deny rules require explicit allow exceptions for keystore unwrap on critical services 3) add a preflight check that runs decision-level unwraps against all control-plane replicas before merges that change deny precedence 4) add a transient cached-unwrapped material fallback in rotator with very short ttl for 30s during RBAC churn
may: ops note: add automated smoke test to CI that rotates a key alias and verifies unwraps from each region and every control-plane replica, plus RBAC permutations (allow, deny, group changes)
oncall: oncall will keep incident open for 2 hours for close monitoring. created blameless incident summary and scheduled a 30m post-incident sync at 09:00 UTC
erin: will draft the blameless writeup with audit decision_ids and KMS grant ids. huge help everyone :heart:
